note: Rust backend module organization map (#task:2265). Machine-readable classification authority consumed by the organization gates. Two axes: business_owner + structural_role. Every crate-root scanned is a row with independently-derived source_shape (file|directory|hybrid) and a STRICT tagged union: exactly one of target:{business_owner,structural_role} (settled) or split_required (residual). split_required is a kind-tagged object: directory_members (groups with members[] closed against the directory mod decls), file_responsibilities (logical grouping of a single large file, no child modules), or hybrid (a <m>.rs main body plus <m>/ production children — both child_groups closed against codec decls AND a non-empty file_responsibilities). This JSON is the ONLY classification authority the gates read; do not copy target allowlists elsewhere. `resolved_splits` records completed large-file responsibilities at their real final leaves and is closed against the source tree by the gate. The 33-table half is closed against the replayed final schema; the non-table half is an OPEN presence ledger. impl_status (rust_writer_known | ts_only | no_known_writer) reflects AUDITED KNOWN writers — human-audited (path,function) evidence, not an exhaustive static proof; the gate does not run a SQL analyzer (see writers_note). Consumes the frozen #2267 (scope_events) and #2268 (daemon_delivery/daemon_events) owner splits. See docs/rust-backend-ddd-context-map-v1.md for the DDD rationale (that document links here for ownership; this JSON is authoritative).

migration_ledger.note: Organization residual/landed is derived, NOT stored. A settled crate_root carries a full physical_target Rust module path: a normal row targets crate::namespace::leaf, while a self-named top-level context root targets its own path crate::module (already at its target). Beside embedded_bootstrap / workspace_data_plane / host_runtime, the landed backend-server roots now include application_orchestration (#2269), conversation_messaging, foundation, identity_access and viewer_read_model (#2270). A split row is residual by construction and its GROUPS carry only target_parent_namespace (crate::owner-ns) + needs_ruling. Completed large-file splits leave the crate-root universe and move to resolved_splits, whose final leaf paths are checked against real declared modules. A root is LANDED iff its current full path equals its physical_target; residual = scanned roots - landed (from the map + real tree only). The CP root inventories in host_agent_scaffold.rs keep their original G4/G5 seam semantics and are used only as a root-coverage compatibility check, never as a landed/residual authority. Route/product ledgers stay separate.

target_namespaces.note: The real Rust module namespace each business_owner relocates into. physical_target is a full path crate::namespace::leaf. landed is derived mechanically (current full path == physical_target); no row is landed until it actually resides at its full target path. Namespaces must be legal Rust idents, unique, and cover exactly the business_owner axis.

writers_note: audited_rust_writers / audited_ts_writers are KNOWN, human-audited write callsites (path + function), NOT an exhaustive static proof of every writer. impl_status = rust_writer_known | ts_only | no_known_writer reflects that audited evidence. Exhaustive write-ownership enforcement is a named residual for a future typed write-perimeter production refactor (see residual_notes); this map does not run a SQL static analyzer.
residual_notes: Exhaustive Rust SQL-write ownership is NOT enforced by this map/gate; it is deferred to a future production refactor that converges all writes behind a typed UnitOfWork / single DB write perimeter, where the invariant can be carried by types or one gate rather than a test-time static analyzer.
